claim: The NETFRAMEWORK guard suppresses ExcludeFromCodeCoverage on every .NET Framework target, including .NET Framework 4.x where ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute is available. Consequently, generated formatters and resolvers compiled for a supported target such as net472 are not decorated, contrary to the requirement that all generated code be decorated except where conditional emission is needed for compilation.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.NetFrameworkGeneratedCodeCoverageAttributeTests.NetFrameworkGeneratedCodeIncludesAvailableAttribute. It generates a formatter and resolver against the net472 reference assemblies with NETFRAMEWORK and NET472 defined and asserts that every generated source contains the attribute. It fails on head because the NETFRAMEWORK branch removes it, even though the attribute exists in .NET Framework 4.7.2. The same guard appears in all the changed templates.

claim: The NETSTANDARD2_0/NETFRAMEWORK guard removes ExcludeFromCodeCoverage on targets where the attribute is actually available (it is supported by .NET Standard 2.0 and .NET Framework 4.0+). Consequently, generated code for those supported targets still affects coverage, contrary to the unconditional requirement; the README's availability explanation is also incorrect. The same guard is repeated across the formatter, union, enum, string-key, and resolver templates.

receipt_plan.detail: Generate and compile a formatter against netstandard2.0 and a supported .NET Framework target (for example net462), then inspect the emitted formatter type for System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute. The compilation demonstrates availability, and the missing attribute demonstrates the requirement gap; repeat for one resolver to cover the shared guard pattern.

claim: The tests only require each generated file to contain at least one attribute, so ResolverTemplate can lose the ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attribute on FormatterCache<T> (and likewise on GetFormatterHelper) while both new tests still pass: the enclosing resolver's attribute remains, and deleting an attribute also deletes its guarded occurrence from the counts.

claim: CompositeResolverTemplate's nested FormatterCache<T> attribute is not independently covered; deleting it leaves the composite resolver class itself decorated, so the per-file Contains assertion and aggregate guard-count assertion both remain green.

claim: The unrelated constraint-dependent brace/newline change in EmitNestingTypesAndNamespaces has no assertion in the new tests, and RunGeneratorAsync discards both the updated compilation and generator diagnostics. Malformed constrained generated syntax could therefore pass CodeCoverageExclusionTests, which inspect only attribute text.
